Learn about extended prompt caching. FAQ Plans and usageBilling and paymentsManaging your plan Plans and usage What do I get with Claude Pro? The Pro plan gives you everything in a Free plan with more usage and more of Claude's capabilities. That includes Claude Code, along with projects to organize your chats and documents, access to more Claude models, and Claude for Microsoft 365. You can choose a monthly or annual subscription. How are Max and Ultra different from Pro? Max and Ultra are built for people who work with Claude throughout the day and want longer, uninterrupted sessions. You get everything in Pro, plus more usage. Max gives you 5x the usage of Pro, every 5 hours and every week. Ultra gives you 10x the weekly usage of Pro, with no 5-hour limit for verified accounts. Both plans include Fable, our top model, for up to half your weekly limit, and a monthly API credit to build on the Claude Platform: $100 on Max, $200 on Ultra. Both plans are billed monthly. See the cards above for current pricing. What are the usage limits on each plan, and what happens when I hit them? Every plan has usage limits. Most accounts have a limit that resets on a rolling five-hour session window, and paid plans add weekly limits on top. Your activity across Claude on web, desktop, mobile, and Claude Code all draws from the same pool. How much you can do depends on the length and complexity of your conversations, the model you choose, and the features you use, so there's no fixed message count. Free covers everyday questions. Pro gives you at least 5x more usage per 5-hour session than Free. Max gives you 5x the usage of Pro every 5 hours and every week. Ultra gives you 10x the weekly usage of Pro, with no 5-hour limit for verified accounts. On Team plans, Standard seats give more than Pro and Premium seats give 5x more than Standard. To manage capacity and make sure all users have fair access, we may limit your usage in other ways, such as weekly and monthly caps or model and feature usage, at our discretion. When you reach a limit, you can wait for it to reset, move to a higher plan, or, on paid plans, turn on usage credits to keep working at standard API rates. You can see where you stand anytime in Settings > Usage. Is Claude Code included in my plan? Claude Code is included in all paid plans. It shares the same usage limits as the rest of your plan, so your work in the terminal and your chats draw from one pool. For heavy coding sessions, you can also switch to pay-as-you-go API credits through a Console account. How much does the Claude Enterprise plan cost? The Claude Enterprise plan is built for large businesses operating at scale. Pricing is $20 per seat per month plus usage billed at API rates, so cost scales with the models and tasks your team runs. Enterprise is billed annually and includes everything in Team plus advanced security and admin controls, including SCIM, audit logs, custom data retention, and role-based access. You can get started self-serve or contact sales for a tailored quote. Billing and payments Can I pay annually? Does it cost less than if I pay monthly? Yes, annual plans are designed to cost less than monthly subscriptions. Annual subscriptions are available for Pro and Team plans. Enterprise plans are only available as annual subscriptions. When you choose to pay annually, you're billed once up front for the year. If you're already on a monthly plan, you can switch to annual in Settings > Billing, and any unused time is credited toward your first annual invoice. See the steps for Pro and Team. Does Claude offer refunds? Payments are generally non-refundable, except where our Consumer Terms of Service say otherwise or where local law requires it. Customers outside of Europe can follow this process to request a refund: Log in, open Get help from the menu, start a message, and choose Claude Refund Request to check your eligibility. If you subscribed through the App Store, Apple handles the refund, so you'll request it from Apple. If you subscribed through Google Play, contact our Support team to check eligibility for an active subscription. If you're in the European Economic Area and the United Kingdom, and within your 14-day withdrawal period, you can request a refund directly in the app. Managing your plan How do I upgrade, downgrade, or switch between plans? You can change your plan any time in Settings. For individual plans, go to Settings > Billing and choose Manage subscription. On Team plans, an Owner or Primary Owner manages this under Organization settings > Billing. See more details here. Upgrades take effect right away, and any unused time on your current plan is credited toward the new one, so you won't pay twice for the same days. Moving from monthly to annual works the same way, with your remaining time credited to the first annual invoice. In some upgrades (for example Pro Annual to Max Monthly), your remaining value on your old plan is larger than the cost of one billing period of the new plan. In this case, the excess will be stored as credit, which will automatically get used for future purchases. Downgrades take effect at the end of your current billing period, and your chats, projects, and files stay with your account whichever plan you're on. How do I cancel my Claude subscription? You can cancel anytime, and your plan stays active until the end of your current billing period. To avoid the next charge, cancel at least 24 hours before your renewal date. If you signed up on the web or the desktop app, go to Settings > Billing and click Cancel. If you subscribed through the App Store or Google Play, cancel from that app under Billing > Manage subscription, or directly in your Apple or Google Play account. Team and self-serve Enterprise: an Owner or Primary Owner cancels under Organization settings > Billing. Sales-assisted Enterprise: Reach out to your Anthropic Contact or our Sales team to discuss cancellation. Canceling doesn't delete your data. Your chats, projects, and files stay with your account, though some features aren't available on the Free plan. For Pro, Max, and Ultra, your account moves to the Free plan once the period ends. For step-by-step help, see how to cancel a Pro, Max, or Ultra plan or cancel a Team plan. Does Claude offer volume discounts? Yes, Claude Enterprise and Claude API pricing can be customized for your organization with volume and committed-spend discounts through our sales team. We don't publish discount rates, so figures you see elsewhere may not reflect our pricing. Built for enterprises: Simplify administration with centralized billing, SSO, enterprise security controls, and more. Common Questions How does Kiro pricing work? How does Kiro pricing work? Kiro offers flexible pricing tiers designed around how developers use Kiro. New users can start with the perpetual Kiro Free tier, which includes 50 credits per month. The Free Tier includes access to open weight models and Claude Sonnet 4.5, with limits. You can upgrade to paid tiers ranging from Pro ($20/month), Pro+ ($40/month), Pro Max ($100/month), to Power ($200/month) for increased capacity. Paid tiers allow purchasing add-on credits to continue using Kiro beyond plan limits. Plans for teams (of 2 and more) are available for $20/seat/month and come with 500 included credits per seat with an option to purchase credits at $0.04 per add-on credit. Kiro prices shown do not include applicable taxes or duties (such as VAT or sales tax) unless explicitly noted. Note that if you have a Japanese billing address, Japanese Consumption Tax will apply to your Kiro usage. The amount of tax collected depends on many factors, including, but not limited to, your Tax Registration Number ("TRN" or Tax ID), and billing address. Kiro in GovCloud pricing is approximately 20% higher than commercial pricing and does not include the Free tier. Kiro processes paid subscriptions on the 1st day of each calendar month. Which models does Kiro use under the hood? Which models does Kiro use under the hood? By default, your prompts are processed by Auto, an agent that uses a mix of different frontier models, combined with specialized models that are experts in specific tasks, intent detection, caching, and other techniques to give you a better balance of quality, latency, and costs. You can also choose a specific model, including OpenAI's GPT-5.6 (Sol, Terra, and Luna), Anthropic's Claude models (Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5), xAI's Grok 4.7, and open weight models such as Kimi K3, DeepSeek 3.2, MiniMax M2.5, GLM-5, and Qwen3 Coder Next. See the [models page](/docs/models) for the full list and current credit multipliers. How does the free trial work? How does the free trial work? The first time you upgrade from Kiro Free to Pro, the rest of that month is free, and you get 500 trial credits to use within 12 months. Plan fees and credits are prorated to the second, so you get plan credits for the time left in the month, and your first bill arrives on the 1st of the following month. Trial credits are used after you run out of plan credits. Upgrading to a paid subscription requires a valid credit card. For example, if you upgrade to Pro ($20/month) at 00:00 UTC on the 15th of a 30-day month, 16 days remain: your prorated fee is $10.67, which the free month covers, so you pay $0 and get 533 plan credits plus 500 trial credits. If you start on Pro+, Pro Max, or Power instead, the free Pro month still counts, and you pay only the difference between your plan's prorated price and the prorated Pro price (for example, $10.67 for Pro+ in the same scenario). If you go back to Kiro Free, your unused trial credits carry over, but you can only spend them on free-tier models. The free trial applies only to your first upgrade. If you upgrade again later, your fee and credits are prorated as usual, without a free month. If you upgraded before November 1, you keep the $20 discount and your unused credits. What is a credit? What is a credit? A credit is a unit of work in response to user prompts. Simple prompts can consume less than 1 credit. More complex prompts, such as executing a spec task, typically cost more than 1 credit. Additionally, different models consume credits at different rates, with a prompt executed via Sonnet 4.6 costing more credits than executing it with Auto. For example, a given task that consumes X credits to execute in Auto, will cost you 1.3X credits to execute via Sonnet 4.6. Credits are metered to the second decimal point, so the least number of credits a task can consume is 0.01 credits. What can I use credits for? What can I use credits for? Any prompt you ask Kiro to execute, whether in vibe mode or spec mode, as well as spec refinement, task execution, and agent hook execution, will consume credits. How can I track my credit usage? How can I track my credit usage? You can see the monthly credit limits for your plan, the number of credits used, and credits remaining in your subscription dashboard accessible in Kiro. Credit usage is updated at least every 5 minutes. For credit pooling, credit usage can be tracked via admin dashboards. How do Kiro workflows affect credit usage? How do Kiro workflows affect credit usage? [Workflows](/docs/workflows/) use the same Kiro credit model as other agent work. Credit usage depends on the agent work they run, so more complex workflows can use more credits. You can guide how Kiro divides the work through your prompt or [steering](/docs/steering/). Kiro currently reports credit usage through your existing account usage view. Can I buy more credits? Can I buy more credits? Yes — how it works depends on your plan: **When signing in with social login or AWS Builder ID (Pro, Pro+, Pro Max, Power):** Purchase add-on credits to continue working. Credits cost $0.04 each, are billed immediately when you buy a pack, and you control exactly how much extra capacity to add. Packs range from $5 (125 credits) to $100. Unused add-on credits roll over and expire 12 months from the date of purchase. See [Add-on credits](/docs/billing/add-on-credits/) for details. **Teams and Enterprise:** With credit pooling, admins can set thresholds at user or pool level, and purchase add-on credits for the pool at any point at $0.04 per credit. Credit pooling doesn’t use overages. Existing Enterprise customers on Pro, Pro+, Pro Max, or Power subscriptions can continue to use [overages](/docs/enterprise/subscription-management/#enable-overages-for-kiro-users). Can I share my Kiro subscription with my team? Can I share my Kiro subscription with my team? For team and enterprise usage, the default pricing model now uses credit pooling. Admins can purchase seats and assign 2 or more seats to a credit pool. Each seat adds 500 included credits per month to the pool and all seat holders in a pool can share credits. Learn about [team billing and management features](/docs/enterprise/billing/). With which tools can I use my Kiro subscription? With which tools can I use my Kiro subscription? Kiro subscriptions can be used with Kiro IDE, Kiro CLI, Kiro Web, Kiro for iOS and Android apps, Kiro Crew, ACP compatible IDEs, and automation in software development (ex: reviews during CI/CD). Use through third-party automation harnesses (such as OpenClaw) that route requests outside of Kiro's native interfaces is not permitted. What happens if I don’t use all my monthly credits? What happens if I don’t use all my monthly credits? For individual subscriptions, usage limits reset at the start of each billing month. Unused credits do not roll over to the next month. For credit pooling, unused included credits expire at the end of the monthly cycle. Any add-on credits that are added by the admin to the pool have a 12-month expiry after purchase. What is Kiro credit pooling? What is Kiro credit pooling? Credit pooling is Kiro’s new pricing model for teams and enterprise customers that allows admins to share Kiro credits across teams. Admins purchase credit pooling seats at $20/seat/month and assign 2 or more seats to a credit pool that is shared by the assigned seats. For each seat assigned to a pool, 500 credits are added to the pool each month. Those credits are prioritized for use by any seat holder assigned to that pool. The admin can add more credits to the pool at $0.04 per credit and those add-on credits have 12-month expiry. What is the difference between included credits and add-on credits? What is the difference between included credits and add-on credits? The $20 per seat per month fee is an access fee for a credit pool. Every seat assignment to a pool adds 500 included credits to the pool. These included credits are available for use each month that the seat exists. Unused included credits do not roll over month-to-month. Add-on credits purchased by admins at $0.04 per credit roll over month over month and can be used for 12 months. How is credit pooling different from individual subscription tiers? How is credit pooling different from individual subscription tiers? Credit pooling pricing is for teams and enterprise customers only. It allows admins to set up Kiro credit pools sharable across seats that admins can assign to team members in a group. There are no individual subscription tiers in the credit pooling pricing model. For individual developers who would like to purchase Kiro subscriptions, the existing tiered pricing of Free, Pro, Pro+, Pro Max, and Power remain available. Why should my team use Kiro credit pooling? Why should my team use Kiro credit pooling? Developers consume credits at different rates. With pooling, heavy users can draw on credits that lighter users don’t need, reducing waste and unnecessary add-on purchases. Teams get more flexibility to accommodate changing usage patterns without having to manage individual credit allowances. Kiro credit pooling enables cost-efficient use of credits across teams. How can administrators monitor and control credit pooling across teams? How can administrators monitor and control credit pooling across teams? Administrators can organize users into groups, assign them to credit pools, and set usage limits for individuals, groups, and profiles. They maintain visibility on user credit, pool credit, and seat utilization via dashboards and get alerts when utilization levels reach 80% and 100% so that they can purchase add-on credits for the pool. Administrators can manage Kiro credit usage with clear policies, real-time enforcement, and automated guardrails. Also, they can choose to create groups for power users and set high credit usage limits for those groups to meet power usage. Light and regular users of Kiro credits can continue to access Kiro independently at lower group-level or individual-level limits without being affected by power users’ credit consumption.
